item.text: I found a config application ordering issue relevant to the standalone Kubernetes service: its legacy `enabled: no` block is applied earlier, but shorthand should override it if proxy config says so. I’ll implement conflict validation when nested Kubernetes is enabled, allow explicitly disabled nested config alongside shorthand, issue the missing-listener warning during config application, and make client fallback replace unspecified bind hosts with the web proxy host.

The code changes are in place and the focused Go tests are compiling; the compiler emitted an existing SQLite C warning. I’m adding coverage for shorthand activation/default port, conflict and disabled-block precedence, plus unspecified-host client resolution, then I’ll rerun the affected test packages.

item.text:
Implemented `proxy_service.kube_listen_addr` shorthand with Kubernetes proxy activation, the default Kubernetes port, and validation that rejects combining it with an enabled legacy Kubernetes block. An explicitly disabled legacy block can coexist with the shorthand, which takes precedence.

Also added a warning when the standalone Kubernetes service and proxy are both enabled without a proxy Kubernetes listen address. Client address resolution now substitutes the web proxy host when the Kubernetes address uses an unspecified or loopback host. Configured public Kubernetes addresses retain priority.

Added shorthand parsing and conflict tests. `go test ./lib/config ./lib/client` passes; `git diff --check` is clean. The build emitted a warning from the existing SQLite C source.
